messages:
alex: FYI acme tenant opened a support ticket — p95 jumped from 120ms -> ~900ms over the last hour. Their app hit a bunch of 504s. Can we triage? :alarm_clock:

sara: on it, looking at traces now. any suspect deploys? :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy completed by @ci for service/inference-runtime at 7198762200 (commit: 9f3a2d). Canary healthy at 5m.

mike: correlating with infra metrics — eviction_count on kv-prefix-cache spiked at 7198763000, per-shard. eviction_rate went from 5/s -> 120/s for shard-17. p95 across shard-17 matches customer region.

tara: customer says this started after the morning deploy. their traffic pattern is high-cardinality session headers. they saw repeated cold starts.

sara: can you paste a sample request header from the ticket? suspect key normalization.

alex: ticket sample: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood-dev.net
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
X-Client-Session: sess-AB12CD34
X-Client-Session: sess-AB12CD34 ; duplicate header variations sometimes
X-Tenant: acme-corp
```

mike: aha — seeing header permutations causing different prefix keys: we index cache keys with all headers currently. small header noise creates millions of pseudo-keys, causing warmup + eviction thrash.

sara: repro plan: spin a small load that mimics session header entropy (randomize X-Client-Session and small variations), run against canary and baseline and watch prefix-unique-key count. if we reproduce, mitigation options: key normalization, TTL increase, or temporary sticky routing to nodes with cold caches.

ops-bot: shard map: shard-17 hosts inference-worker-17,18; mem pressure on worker-17 = 78%, worker-18 = 83% (7198764600).

mike: quick mitigation I can push: 1) increase prefix-cache TTL from 30s -> 5m for affected tenants (soft config) 2) enable header-normalization flag (strip ephemeral headers) as a rollout to canary 3) if still bad, route acme to dedicated pool. Which first?

sara: do 1 + 2 to canary. 1 buys time. 2 reduces new cardinality. 3 is escalation.

alex: approved. mike, can you also add a short-term rate limiter on novel-prefix-per-minute to avoid stampede?

mike: added limiter to canary at 7198765020, throttle threshold 50 novel prefixes/min for tenant. logging enabled.

tara: letting customer know we're rolling mitigations now. will give ETA 30m.

sara: repro notes for the ticket (copying here):
```
# repro steps
1) curl -X POST https://canary.api.redwood-dev.net/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Tenant: acme-corp" \
  -H "X-Client-Session: sess-$(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
2) run at ~200rps for 10 minutes with randomized header suffixes (case, trailing spaces)
3) observe prefix_unique_keys metric and p95 latency for shard-17
```

mike: early results after TTL bump + normalization flag on canary: prefix_unique_keys down 78%, p95 for acme routed to canary down from 900ms -> 160ms. still watching for p99 tail.

alex: awesome. next steps: mike to prepare a patch to normalize header set deterministically in runtime (strip duplicates, normalize case, drop ephemeral headers) + e2e test. sara to monitor customer p99 for 2 hours and confirm. tara to update the support ticket with mitigation notes and ETA for permanent fix.

sara: noted. I'll keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
